falsifiable_hypothesis: The verified A-side auxiliary correction is intentionally smaller than the primary B-side correction. Fitting-only inner estimates frequently saturate the negative A bound while the positive bound is already an effective guardrail. A single globally fixed negative extension of exactly 2*PRIOR=0.25 preserves the positive cap, avoids any fold or target routing, and tests whether the former symmetric bound was clipping stable negative correction signal.
B_rule: Reproduce prior_floor_halfvote_dual_gain exactly for orientation B: detect global gain signal using [1,3], deploy raw gain clipped to [0.75,3] when the positive-part global gain reliability is positive, otherwise use its frozen fallback.
A_rule: Reproduce prior_floor_halfvote_dual_gain A-side fitting, bounded-jackknife reliability, global positive-part reliability, r_A^3 base confirmation, and two-of-three halfway / three-of-three full vote-strength confirmation. Change only the globally fixed raw A gain bound from [-0.5,0.5] to [-0.75,0.5], where -0.75=-0.5-2*PRIOR and PRIOR=0.125. Apply qA=qA_loo_bagged+0.5*gA_final*theta. The same bounds apply to every target and every outer fold.
bound_rationale: The extension is one prefrozen algebraic step of two existing PRIOR units on only the previously clipped negative side; the positive +0.5 guardrail remains untouched. This family was proposed after development diagnostics and is not independent validation.

task_contract.ab_rule: average losses across separately costed A/B orientations; never average predictions
